title: Midyear Transparency Week - talk notes & Q/A scratch
content:
Purpose / framing:
- Quick scratchpad for CEO + exec segment during "Transparency Week" (midyear). Not polished — raw notes for rehearsal.
- Goal: acknowledge progress, call out tradeoffs (cost/latency/quality), be candid about incidents and mitigation, and surface commitments for next 90 days.

Opening (30s):
- Hi team — short, honest update. We launched Dedicated last year and it unlocked big customer work, but it also exposed gaps in our monitoring and handoffs. Today is about what we learned and what we will fix.

Top-line metrics to call out (30s):
- API success rate (p50/p95 errs): current: success 99.3% (target 99.9) — trending up since Feb rollouts.
- Avg token cost per 1k: down 12% YOY (batching + quant recommendations).
- Latency SLOs: p95 steady ~420ms on hosted for small models; spikes remain in heavy-burst windows.

What we screwed up (candor section, 60s):
- Incident recap high level: late-Jan capacity blip due to autoscaler regression + slow fallback policy. Impact: some customers saw elevated latencies and throttles for ~3 hours.
- Why it happened: autoscaler config shipped w/ conservative headroom; fallback routing defaulted to a variant with incompatible tokenizer.
- What we did: fast rollback, emergency patch for routing policy, postmortem started (JIRA-OPS-3421).

What customers heard / felt (short):
- Concern about reliability & predictability. Some customers considered contingency plans. We should own that.

Concrete commitments (30-45s):
- Commitment 1: Reliability SLO roadmap — we will hit 99.9% platform success rate for paid tiers by end of Q3. (Owner: SRE)
- Commitment 2: Predictable fallback flows — ensure tokenizers/compatibility checks in routing policy before any automated fallback. (Owner: Serving Runtime)
- Commitment 3: Transparency cadence — weekly incident summaries for customers with dedicated capacity + internal "hot recap" emails for PM/SE teams. (Owner: Customer Success)

Tough Q&A (prep shorthand):
Q: "Is our infra fundamentally overloaded?"
A: Not fundamentally — capacity grows with demand. The root was misconfigured autoscaling thresholds for a specific pool and failure path in fallback policy. We're increasing safety headroom and improving pre-deploy chaos checks.

Q: "Will costs go up to reach the SLOs?"
A: Short term there will be modest incremental spend for burst capacity and better observability; mid-term improvements (smarter batching, cache rules) will reduce unit cost per token. We will share expected delta in next week's cost brief.

Q: "How do we prevent regressions like the tokenizer mismatch?"
A: Add compatibility gating in routing logic + automated integration tests that run against model variants and tokenizers. Also a lightweight canary for fallback flows. (Owner: Platform Engineering)

Notes to speaker (bullet-clipped):
- Use specific customer-safe language — e.g., "some customers experienced higher latency" vs listing names.
- Call out the team wins (Reduce token cost 12%) before diving into what went wrong — gives context that we're improving overall.
- Keep tone: accountable, not defensive.

Follow-ups / internal TODOs (scratch):
- Leah: draft the "customer-facing incident explainer" by 2026-03-08 (linked to CONFLUENCE-TRNS-789).
- Arman: schedule the reliability playbook sync with SRE + Serving Runtime (week of 3/9).
- Ops: run targeted chaos test on fallback routing (add to release pipeline).

Open questions (raw):
- Do we want a permanent "Transparency Week" staple after this? pros/cons? (cost of prep vs value of trust)
- Should we include a short live demo showing tracing dashboard or keep it verbal? Demo adds time + fragility.

Slack / comms pointers (quick):
- Pre-share a 1-pager with TL;DR to #all-hands 24-48h before. Avoid surprises.
- Prepare a canned reply for customer support for the top 3 concerns (latency, cost, SLA).

Draft short closing line: "We will fix what broke, share updates weekly, and keep building. Thank you for the work and for pushing us to be better — transparency is how we earn trust."

Scratch notes / rehearsal hints:
- Pause after commitments so listeners can absorb.
- Expect 2 live tough questions; have backup data handy (p50/p95 trend charts, cost delta estimate).

References / links (raw IDs):
- Incident postmortem draft: JIRA-OPS-3421
- Customer explainer draft: CONFLUENCE-TRNS-789
- Fallback routing PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2567

Last thought (personal):
- Keep it short. People remember two things: the apology + the plan. Make sure both are crystal.

-- end of scratchpad --
